# Topic {.unnumbered}

## Project Description {.unnumbered}

**Public Valuation of Publicly Funded Research**

In 2025, the Dutch Research Council (NWO), spent 1.3 billion euros on research funding (NWO, 2026). In the same year, the European Research Council (ERC), the main public body for research funding in Europe, made more than 2.7 billion euros available for research grants (European Research Council, 2024). National and regional research councils receive their budget primarily from national governments, funded in turn by taxation on private citizens and businesses. While research suggests that public funding of science tends to align with what the public uses and benefits from at the aggregate level (Yin et al., 2022), it remains unclear whether individual citizens themselves notice this, too.

In this project, you will explore how the public values the projects it pays for, and what factors shape these judgments. Together with other students, you will collect experimental and self-report data via an online task and select a subset of variables to test your hypothesis.

## Literature Suggestions {.unnumbered}

Below are literature suggestions that can help you get acquainted with some variables that will be included in the study. The list is not comprehensive - it serves as a little introduction into the larger topic.

Consider these papers a starting point for choosing your research question(s), and search for additional relevant literature after.

::: hanging
